name: Take a push
purpose: The first task that cannot be solved by memorising a pose - the robot has to notice it was shoved and do something. That makes it the first real use of the potentiometers, and it builds the reflex walking needs, where every step is a disturbance the robot creates for itself.
bar: Survives repeated shoves from any direction over 20 s, on ground anywhere from slippery to grippy, with mass and servo gains varied.
notes: 256 robots at once, 50 Hz control. Shoves 0.4-1.2 m/s from any angle, spin 1.5 rad/s.

scoring.name: fell_over
scoring.what: Fell. By far the largest single number here, and the one thing that ends an attempt.

scoring.name: height
scoring.what: Trunk at the ride height. 1.0 dead on, falling away over 30 mm.

scoring.name: tilt
scoring.what: Trunk off level. Measured off gravity, so it needs no outside reference.

scoring.name: skidding
scoring.what: A foot sliding along the floor while it is carrying weight. Nothing stopped the robot recovering by scuffing its feet across the ground, and that does not survive contact with a real floor: the simulator's friction is a guess, and a policy that leans on sliding is leaning on the guess.

scoring.name: end_stops
scoring.what: Driving a joint into the last few degrees of its travel. On the real robot that is a servo straining against a hard stop.

scoring.name: posture
scoring.what: Joints near the stance they started in, rather than any pose that happens to stay up.

scoring.name: still
scoring.what: Trunk not moving. Standing still means still, not slowly drifting.

scoring.name: alive
scoring.what: A small amount for every moment it has not fallen. Stops it ending an attempt early to escape a bad score.

scoring.name: foot_lift
scoring.what: Picking a foot up and putting it down. Once sliding is expensive, the only way left to move a foot is to lift it - this pays for doing that properly rather than dragging.

scoring.name: spinning
scoring.what: Trunk rotating. A shove usually sets the robot turning as well as sliding, and killing that rotation is most of recovering from it. The stand task had no term for this because nothing ever span it.

scoring.name: twitching
scoring.what: How much the commanded angles jump between one moment and the next. Smooth commands are the single biggest factor in whether this survives contact with a real servo.

scoring.name: effort
scoring.what: Total torque across the twelve joints. Keeps the pose inside what a 20 kg-cm servo can hold, and saves battery.

scoring.name: joint_speed
scoring.what: Joints moving at all. A robot standing still should be still.
